# The code: where it is and what it does

> **Status: experiments, as of 25 Oct 2026.** The site publishes the design; the code lives in one repository, [SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI), and today it carries the first four experiments, not a component. This page is the map: the package, its modules, the commands, and where each thing on this site has code behind it.

## Where everything is

| What | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| the `sharness-ai` package | [`sharness_ai/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/tree/dev/sharness_ai) on the `dev` branch; v0.1.0 on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/sharness-ai/) carries only `--version` | runnable from the repository; unreleased |
| the experiments, numbered | [`experiments/README.md`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md) | E01 to E04 runnable; E05 to E08 planned |
| the example policies | [`experiments/policies/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/tree/dev/experiments/policies) | runnable |
| the skill for a Claude Code session | [`.claude/skills/sharness-hello/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/.claude/skills/sharness-hello/SKILL.md) | runnable |
| the tests | [`tests/unit/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/tree/dev/tests/unit), 40 tests; Landlock tests skip where it is absent | green on 25 Oct 2026 |
| the ground rules for agents working in the repository | [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/CLAUDE.md) | |
| the release pipeline | [`.github/workflows/workflow.yml`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/.github/workflows/workflow.yml): tests, version bump, tag, PyPI by Trusted Publishing | runs on a push to `main` |
| the browser mockups | this site, [`explain/mockups/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__Website/tree/dev/explain/mockups): hand-written HTML, no build | published |
| the storyboards' data | this site, [`content/storyboards/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__Website/tree/dev/content/storyboards) | published |
| this site's build tools | [`tools/`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__Website/tree/dev/tools): the generators and the gate, Python standard library and Node | |

## The package, module by module

Standard library only. Each module is meant to be read in one sitting; the design's size targets are launcher ≤ 400 lines, each component ≤ 300, a shared library ≤ 400.

| Module | Lines | Does | Experiment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli.py` | 98 | the argument parser and the dispatch: `probe`, `policy hash`, `policy check`, `run`, `hello` | |
| `probe.py` | 138 | the grant: reads `/proc/self/status`, the Landlock ABI, `memfd_secret`, the namespaces, cgroups, the kernel config, the tools present, the names of proxy variables | E01 |
| `policy.py` | 126 | a v0 policy: load, check the shape (including the caps), canonicalise (sorted keys, no whitespace, integers only), hash | E02 |
| `translate.py` | 176 | the policy as bubblewrap, `docker run`, a Claude Code sandbox `settings.json`, a Kubernetes Pod and NetworkPolicy; each with what it does not enforce | E10 |
| `landlock.py` | 157 | Landlock through `ctypes`: the ABI, a ruleset, path rules, port rules, `restrict_self` | E03 |
| `run.py` | 133 | fork, apply the policy in the child (network namespace, caps, `no_new_privs`, Landlock), exec; `--expect-hash` | E03 |
| `limits.py` | 95 | the caps: `RLIMIT_AS` and `RLIMIT_NPROC`, and a memory and pids cgroup (v1 or v2) where `/sys/fs/cgroup` is writable | E03 |
| `hello.py` | 124 | the acceptance test: a deny-all policy for the running interpreter with a 128 MiB cap, six probes, the caveat | E04 |
| `_version.py` | 17 | the version, read from the file CI maintains | |

Counts from `wc -l` on 25 Oct 2026. How a command moves through these modules is on [Flows](flows/index.md).

## The commands

```
sharness-ai probe [--json]                                E01  the grant
sharness-ai policy hash|check FILE                        E02  the one value the person supplies
sharness-ai policy translate FILE --to T [-- CMD…]        E10  the policy in another enforcer's form, and the gap
sharness-ai run --policy FILE [--expect-hash H] -- CMD…   E03  one command under a policy
sharness-ai hello [--json]                                E04  the acceptance test, one child process
```

Install and use: [The CLI](cli/index.md). Each command's output and caveats: [Examples](examples/index.md). What each shows and does not show: [Mockups and experiments](experiments/index.md).

## What has code behind it, and what does not

| On this site | Code | Where |
|---|---|---|
| the v0 Process Behaviour Policy and its hash | yes | `policy.py`; the [browser mockup](../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html) reproduces it |
| Landlock file, exec and port rules; `network: "none"` | yes | `landlock.py`, `run.py` |
| the grant and the delta | yes | `probe.py` |
| the memo's acceptance test | yes, for one child process | `hello.py` |
| the launcher, `sharness.kms`, `.net`, `.fs`, `.bash`, `.llm` | **no** | designed on [Components](../design/components/index.md); E05 to E08 are the next pieces |
| mutual TLS with a session CA; the edge matrix | measured by hand, not yet a command | E05 |
| memory and process-count caps (rlimits and cgroups) | yes | `limits.py`, measured 25 Oct 2026 |
| seccomp, the `cpu` cgroup, scoping, the execute allowlist | **no** | [Containment](../design/containment/index.md) says which rows are designed |

## Next in the code, in order

The [research note](../evidence/research/index.md#4-what-is-still-open-in-the-order-to-take-it) sets the order: E06 (the process tree), E05 (the edges as a script), E08 (`sharness.kms` v0) before E07 (`sharness.llm` v0), then the launcher as a script above the agent on a laptop. The languages for each are on [Languages](languages/index.md).


==============================================================================
== code/cli/index.md — The CLI
==============================================================================

# The CLI: sharness-ai

> **Status: experiments.** A Python package, `sharness-ai`, that will carry the SHarness launcher and components. Today it carries the first experiments. Source: [SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI). The command is `sharness-ai`.

## What exists, as of 24 Oct 2026

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| [PyPI, v0.1.0](https://pypi.org/project/sharness-ai/) | reports its version and prints its help; also installs a `sharness` shorthand, removed on `dev` |
| the `dev` branch | the proposed scope in the README; `sharness-ai` as the only command; experiments E01 to E04 (`probe`, `policy hash`, `policy check`, `run`, `hello`), their tests, the `sharness-hello` skill. Not released until `dev` is merged to `main` |

```
$ pip install sharness-ai            # v0.1.0: version and help only
$ pip install git+https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI@dev     # the experiments, unreleased
$ sharness-ai --version
sharness-ai v0.1.0
$ sharness-ai
usage: sharness-ai [-h] [--version] command ...
  probe     E01: the grant, what a process here can do before any policy
  policy    E02: hash or check a Process Behaviour Policy (v0)
  run       E03: run one command under a policy (Linux, Landlock)
  hello     E04: the memo's acceptance test, for one child process
```

Requires Python 3.11 or later. No runtime dependencies: Landlock is reached through `ctypes`, hashing through `hashlib`, nothing else is needed. The map of what each experiment shows and does not show is [Mockups and experiments](../experiments/index.md).

## The first version, as proposed

The memo says one CLI project for now, components split out later if one is useful on its own ([roadmap decision 7](../../design/roadmap/index.md#open-decisions)). So the first version of `sharness-ai` is one package whose subcommands are the experiments today and the components tomorrow, in the order the ladder sets:

```
sharness-ai probe                                  E01  the grant                         runnable
sharness-ai policy hash|check FILE                 E02  the one value the person supplies  runnable
sharness-ai run --policy FILE [--expect-hash H] -- CMD…   E03  one command under a policy  runnable
sharness-ai hello                                  E04  the acceptance test, one process   runnable

sharness-ai edges                                  E05  session CA + role certs + the edge matrix      planned
sharness-ai tree                                   E06  the process-tree proof of concept               planned
sharness-ai llm   --listen :port --policy FILE     E07  sharness.llm v0, where ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points  planned
sharness-ai kms   --policy FILE                    E08  sharness.kms v0: init, public, unwrap, seal_to, destroy  planned

sharness-ai launch --manifest m.json --expect-hash sha256:M -- claude …     the launcher: above the agent   designed
```

Three rules for the package, carried from the design:

- **Stdlib only, small modules.** Each module small enough to read in one sitting: the design's targets are launcher ≤ 400 lines, each component ≤ 300, a shared library ≤ 400. `landlock.py` is about 150 lines; `run.py` about 130.
- **Status words in the code too.** `--help` says *experiments*; `hello` prints its caveat every run; nothing says *sandboxed* about the agent.
- **Child subtree only.** Every command that enforces anything forks a child and applies the policy there. The shell you run it from is never restricted. That is the safety rule for testing in a live session, built into the tool.

## The v0 policy

`run` and `hello` take a v0 Process Behaviour Policy: six keys, integers only, hashed as canonical JSON. It is the smallest shape that can be enforced by Landlock and hashed identically by Python and the browser; the full schema is on [Process Behaviour Policies §4](../../design/policies/index.md#4-schema) and v0 grows towards it, never away from it.

```json
{"pbp": 1, "id": "deny-all-example", "layer": "invocation",
 "files":   {"read": ["/usr", "/lib", "/lib64", "/bin", "/etc"], "write": [], "exec": ["/usr", "/bin"]},
 "network": "none",
 "process": {"no_new_privs": true}}
```

Its hash, from `sharness-ai policy hash` and from the [browser mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html): `sha256:ab1d3e4e779313274f7a1d3ef3e46f6eacef038d8cfaa6198151a45cd82dcc76`.

## Why sharness-ai, not sharness

Plain `sharness` is the Debian, pkgsrc and OpenBSD package name of an unrelated shell test library, so SHarness does not use it as a command. `sharness-ai` matches the PyPI distribution. Environment variables use the prefix `SHARNESS_AI_` (proposed); `run` sets `SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_HASH` and `SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_ID` for the child.

## Where the version lives

One file owns it: `sharness_ai/version`. `sharness-ai --version` reads that file at import time; CI writes it, together with the version in `pyproject.toml`, on every release. The same convention as sgit.

## How it is released

Day-to-day work lands on `dev`, the default branch. Merging `dev` into `main` cuts a release: every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/workflow.yml` in the CLI repository.

| Job | What it does |
|---|---|
| Run Unit Tests | `pytest tests/unit` with coverage, on Python 3.11. Tests that need Landlock skip where the kernel lacks it. A failure stops the release |
| Increment Tag | bumps the middle number (`v0.N.0` → `v0.N+1.0`), writes it to the version file, `pyproject.toml` and the README badge, commits, and tags |
| Publish to: PYPI | builds with Poetry and uploads through Trusted Publishing: GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for a short-lived PyPI token, so no API key is stored anywhere |

Why one workflow file: PyPI's trusted publisher for `sharness-ai` is bound to the repository and the workflow filename (`workflow.yml`). The publish job therefore lives in that file, not in a reusable workflow it calls. Renaming the file breaks publishing until the PyPI configuration is updated to match.

## For agents working in the repository

The repository carries a `CLAUDE.md` with the ground rules (status words, threat model, stdlib only, tests, names, releases) and the skill `sharness-hello` that runs E01 and E04 inside a Claude Code session under the design's safety rules.


==============================================================================
== code/experiments/index.md — Mockups and experiments
==============================================================================

# Mockups and experiments

> **Status: experiments.** No SHarness component is built. What is runnable is listed here with where it runs; what was measured carries its date; everything else is planned. The design these experiments test is on the [design pages](../../design/architecture/index.md).

Dinis Cruz's memo of 24 October 2026 sets the method: *start with very simple examples, each component done in isolation, as simple, as fast and as slim as possible; then harden; then test*. This page is that method as a ladder. Each rung is something a person can run, in the browser, in any Claude session, or on a Linux box, and each says what it shows and what it does not.

## The ladder

| Rung | Where it runs | What is on it | Status as of 24 Oct 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **the browser**, nothing installed | the [policy hash mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html) and the [edge matrix mockup](../../explain/mockups/edges.html); the [storyboards](../../explain/storyboards/index.md); E09, a real kernel in a tab running `hello` ([researched](../browser/index.md)) | published; E09 not built |
| 1 | **any Claude session, any laptop** (Python 3.11+) | E01 `sharness-ai probe`, E02 `sharness-ai policy hash`, E10 `sharness-ai policy translate` | runnable |
| 2 | **Linux** (Landlock, 5.13+; TCP rules 6.7+); a Claude Code session via the skill | E03 `sharness-ai run`, E04 `sharness-ai hello` | runnable; E04 measured 24 Oct 2026 |
| 3 | Linux, a checkout, `cryptography` | E05 session CA and the edge matrix over mutual TLS; E06 the process-tree proof of concept; E07 `sharness.llm` v0; E08 `sharness.kms` v0 | planned |
| 4 | a launcher **above** the agent: a script on a laptop, then a platform | the components as `sharness.<role>` processes under one manifest hash | designed |

The rungs are ordered by what they need, not by importance. Rung 4 is the point; rungs 0 to 3 are how to get there without claiming anything before it is true.

## The experiments

Numbered in the CLI repository, [experiments/README.md](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md), where each has its command, its output and its caveats.

| # | Experiment | Shows | Does not show |
|---|---|---|---|
| E01 | `sharness-ai probe`: the **grant**, what a process here can do before any policy: uid, capabilities, `NoNewPrivs`, seccomp, Landlock ABI, `memfd_secret`, namespaces, cgroups, the tools present, whether egress is proxied | the delta in one sentence: in the measured workspace the grant is everything | anything about what a policy would do; it only measures the starting point. Prints the names of proxy variables, never their values |
| E02 | `sharness-ai policy hash`: canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8, integers only) → `sha256:…`, the one value the person supplies; the same hash from the [browser mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html) | two implementations, one hash, so a hash can travel from the person to a launcher out of band | signing by the root key; policy layers composed by intersection; the full schema. The v0 shape is six keys |
| E03 | `sharness-ai run --policy p.json [--expect-hash sha256:…] -- cmd`: one command under a policy: Landlock read, write and exec rules per path; TCP connect per port; `network: "none"` as an empty network namespace where the process may make one, else Landlock denying every TCP bind and connect | a policy enforced by the kernel on a child and all its descendants, and a launcher's first check (the hash) in one flag | seccomp, a separate uid, cgroups, mutual TLS; UDP (Landlock does not see it, so without a namespace DNS still resolves) |
| E04 | `sharness-ai hello`: the memo's acceptance test for one child process: read allowed, write to `/tmp` and to the workspace refused, TCP connect refused, a wrong hash runs nothing; exit 0 when every expectation held | the test the memo asks for, for one process, with the caveat printed as part of the result | that **the agent** is confined: a policy a process applies to its own children is a Boundary for them and a Setting for itself |
| E05 | a script that makes a session CA, four role certificates and checks the edge matrix over mutual TLS (what the design measured by hand) | the edges allowed and denied exactly per the matrix, repeatably | anything new; it makes the measured figures reproducible |
| E06 | the process-tree proof of concept: a mini orchestrator that cannot exec a shell, and a bash server outside its domain | every side door on [Enforcing the process tree](../../design/process-tree/index.md) closed or not | runs only under the [safety rules](../../design/process-tree/index.md#4-safety-rules-for-testing-inside-a-live-agent-session) |
| E07 | `sharness.llm` v0: a Messages API pass-through at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` with a secret filter on every tool result and user message | the transcript leak closed for every tool at once | the real API key via the KMS; that is E08 |
| E08 | `sharness.kms` v0: an identity made in-process, a sealed `m1` opened, derived keys re-sealed to a one-time key, never a clear key printed | the KMS protocol's `unwrap`, end to end, locally | remote binding; hardware keys |
| E09 | the harness in a browser tab: a real 32-bit Linux kernel in v86 (Alpine's `linux-virt`, Landlock on) running `hello`, and a kernel without Landlock as the negative control ([Linux in the browser](../browser/index.md)) | the same syscalls on an emulated CPU, for anyone with a browser | timings; anything about the host; `memfd_secret`'s physical property. Researched, not built |
| E10 | `sharness-ai policy translate FILE --to bwrap\|docker\|claude-code\|kubernetes`: the same policy in another enforcer's form, followed by what that target does not enforce | the policy as the centre and every enforcer as a target; the [enforceability matrix](../../landscape/enforceability/index.md) made executable | enforcement by the target: nothing is run against it here. Runnable |

## E04, measured

Run on 24 October 2026 in one Claude Code cloud session (Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.18, Landlock ABI 7, uid 0, Python 3.13), as of 24 Oct 2026. Method and the JSON are on [Evidence §9](../../evidence/index.md#9-the-first-experiments-run-by-the-cli).

```
$ sharness-ai hello
sharness-ai hello   experiment E04: the memo's acceptance test, for one child process
policy      hello  sha256:ad37e58bea6f4da65656687045b33ae9977caf90feef0ff5716a44db041b35af
            read-only: /bin, /etc, /lib, /lib64, /opt, /sbin, <the workspace>, /usr, /usr/bin
            write: none · exec: system and Python · network: none
kernel      Landlock ABI 7 · empty network namespace: yes (uid 0)
  ✔ read       expected allowed  got allowed
  ✔ write-tmp  expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/tmp/sharness-ai-hello.tmp')
  ✔ write-cwd  expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'sharness-ai-hello.tmp')
  ✔ net        expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied)
  ✔ hash       expected refused  got refused
result      5/5 held
caveat      applied by this process to its own children: a Boundary for them, a Setting for whoever ran
            this, who could have skipped it. The launcher that makes it a Boundary for the agent too is the design.
```

The whole run took 0.6 s. The same policy under E03 with port 443 allowed connected to `1.1.1.1:443` and was refused on port 80, as the policy said.

## Running them in a Claude session

The CLI repository carries a skill, [`sharness-hello`](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/.claude/skills/sharness-hello/SKILL.md), that runs E01 and E04 inside a Claude Code session under the design's [safety rules](../../design/process-tree/index.md#4-safety-rules-for-testing-inside-a-live-agent-session): never touch the orchestrator, never firewall uid 0 or the model API, everything as a child subtree, leave nothing behind. It reports in the site's status words and says, every time, that a policy the session applies to its child does not bind the session.

That is the honest answer to the memo's *maybe even a skill* ([roadmap decision 8](../../design/roadmap/index.md#open-decisions)): a skill can install the CLI, run the experiments and apply a policy to everything the session starts from then on; it cannot apply one to the session itself. Binding the session needs the launcher above it.

## What Claude Code's own sandbox already gives, and what SHarness adds

Claude Code ships a sandbox for shell commands (documented at [code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing), read 24 Oct 2026): on Linux, `bubblewrap` for the filesystem, a separate network namespace, and a proxy outside the sandbox that checks each connection's **hostname** against allowed and denied domains; on macOS, Seatbelt. It is off by default and on with `"sandbox": {"enabled": true}`. The design pages did not mention it; the research behind this release did, and the comparison is useful because the two agree on the mechanism and differ on exactly the points SHarness is about.

| | Claude Code sandbox (as documented 24 Oct 2026) | SHarness (designed) |
|---|---|---|
| What it covers | Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and their children | every process, including the orchestrator: enforced at the root of the process tree |
| Not covered | built-in Read, Edit, Write, WebFetch; hooks; MCP servers; `excludedCommands`; the harness itself | the design's "side doors" list is this list; `sharness.bash` as the only way to run a process is how it closes them |
| Files | writes limited to the working directory and a temp dir; reads of most of the machine, credentials included | per-component, per-subcommand read, write and exec lists; the workspace with no execute right; `sharness.fs` as the only writer |
| Network | a hostname allowlist at a proxy that does not terminate TLS (domain fronting noted as a limit in its own docs) | `sharness.net` **is** the TLS client, so it sees and verifies the name; endpoint and vault-id allowlists; no redirects, no IP literals |
| Secrets | the sandbox does not hold or hide them; the model API key stays with the harness | `sharness.kms` holds them; the harness holds a dummy; `sharness.llm` adds the real key |
| Who decides | settings the user (or a managed policy) sets; `allowUnsandboxedCommands` and the unsandboxed retry are escape hatches by design | one manifest hash the person supplies out of band; the launcher refuses anything else; no retry path |
| Who enforces | the Claude Code process, for its own children | a launcher above the agent; the platform in the end state |

Two conclusions for the design, carried to [Agents and LLMs §2](../../design/agents/index.md#2-where-sharness-plugs-in) and [Policies §9](../../design/policies/index.md#9-prior-art-reuse-dont-rebuild): the sandbox is the natural **transparent** host for `sharness.bash` on a laptop today, and its documented limits are a checklist of what the components add. A SHarness policy should be able to generate the sandbox's settings as one of its enforcement layers, the same way it would generate a Kubernetes `securityContext`.

## What is not here

- **No component.** Every experiment is a probe or a one-process enforcement; `sharness.launcher`, `.kms`, `.net`, `.fs`, `.bash` and `.llm` are designs.
- **One environment.** E04 was measured in one cloud session on one day. A laptop will differ: no root, and on Ubuntu 24.04 an unprivileged user namespace may be refused, so `network: "none"` falls back to Landlock's TCP rules, which do not cover UDP.
- **The browser mockups compute, they do not enforce.** A hash in a browser proves two implementations agree; nothing in a browser can confine a process.

Sources: [experiments/README.md](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md) in the CLI repository; [A secure harness for agents](../../articles/secure-harness-for-agents.md); the Claude Code documentation on [sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing), [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) and [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), read 24 Oct 2026.


==============================================================================
== code/flows/index.md — Flows through the code
==============================================================================

# Flows through the code

> **Status: runnable**, as of 25 Oct 2026, on the CLI's `dev` branch. What happens, module by module and syscall by syscall, when a command is confined and when the acceptance test runs; then the flow the launcher will add, which is designed and not built. Line numbers are from the files on that date and will drift; the function names will not.

## 1. `sharness-ai run --policy p.json --expect-hash sha256:M -- cmd`

```
 cli.main                      parse: --policy, --expect-hash, --verbose, argv after "--"
   │
   ▼
 policy.load(path)             JSON file → dict; refuses non-objects and non-JSON
 policy.check(policy)          the v0 shape: pbp=1, id, files.read/write/exec (absolute paths),
                               network "none" | {connect_tcp_ports}, process.no_new_privs: true
 policy.policy_hash(policy)    canonical bytes (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8, integers only)
                               → "sha256:" + hex                                         ← E02
   │
   ├── expect_hash given and ≠ hash  →  print "refused … Nothing ran.", exit 125
   ├── check found problems          →  exit 125
   ├── landlock.abi() == 0           →  "Landlock is not available", exit 126
   │
   ▼
 run.run: os.fork()
   │
   ├─ parent: waitpid(child) → the child's exit code; removes the child's cgroup
   │
   └─ child: run.apply(policy)
        1. network "none"  → run._unshare_net():  unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)
                               EPERM? → unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET)
                               still refused? → rely on Landlock TCP rules (UDP uncovered)
        1b. caps (process.max_memory_mb, max_pids): limits.cgroup() makes a memory and pids cgroup
                               for this pid where /sys/fs/cgroup is writable; limits.rlimits() sets RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_NPROC
        2. landlock.Ruleset(): landlock_create_ruleset(2) with every fs right the ABI knows,
                               + bind/connect TCP (ABI 4+), + signal/abstract-socket scoping (ABI 6+)
        3. for each path:     landlock_add_rule(2) PATH_BENEATH with O_PATH fd and the rights:
                                 read  → READ_FILE | READ_DIR
                                 exec  → EXECUTE | READ_FILE | READ_DIR
                                 write → every right of the ABI
                               a missing path is skipped and reported; a plain file gets file rights only
           for each port:     landlock_add_rule(2) NET_PORT with CONNECT_TCP
        4. ruleset.restrict_self(): prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1); landlock_restrict_self(2)
                               → final for this process and every descendant, for ever
        5. environ: SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_HASH, SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_ID
        6. os.execvp(cmd)      the command runs under the policy; anything it starts inherits it
           (any failure before exec → stderr, _exit(126))
```

Why fork then apply, and not apply then fork: `restrict_self` is irreversible for the calling process, so it is only ever called in a child. The shell you typed `run` into is never restricted. That is also why the result is a Boundary for the child and a Setting for the caller.

## 2. `sharness-ai hello`

```
 hello.hello()
   │
   ▼
 hello.hello_policy()          a deny-all for *this* interpreter: read and exec the system prefixes,
                               sys.base_prefix and the interpreter's directory; read the workspace;
                               write nothing; network "none"
 policy.policy_hash()          printed, so the person can keep it
   │
   ▼
 write the policy to a temporary file
 for each probe (read, write-tmp, write-cwd, net, memory):
     subprocess: python -m sharness_ai run --policy <tmp> -- python -I -c <probe>     ← the flow above, end to end
     hello._classify(): "allowed" if the probe printed ok; "refused (…)" on PermissionError / OSError
 one more:  run … --expect-hash sha256:000… → must be refused with "Nothing ran" (exit 125)
   │
   ▼
 compare against EXPECT; print the table, "N/5 held", and the caveat
 delete the temporary policy; exit 0 if every expectation held
```

`hello` deliberately goes through the CLI (`python -m sharness_ai run`) rather than calling `run.run` in-process, so the acceptance test exercises the same path a person types.

## 3. `sharness-ai probe`

`probe.probe()` reads `/proc/self/status` (uid, capability sets, `NoNewPrivs`, `Seccomp`), calls `landlock_create_ruleset(2)` with the version flag to get the ABI, tries `memfd_secret(2)` (syscall 447) and closes the fd, lists `/proc/self/ns`, looks at `/sys/fs/cgroup`, reads the relevant keys from `/proc/config.gz`, checks which tools are on the path, and lists the *names* of proxy variables that are set. `probe.render()` prints it as text; `--json` prints the dict. Nothing is written.

## 4. The policy hash, in two implementations

```
 Python (policy.canonical)                       Browser (explain/mockups/policy-hash.html)
   refuse floats                                   refuse non-integers
   json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True,                 keys sorted by code point, recursively;
     separators=(",", ":"),                        JSON.stringify for strings, integers, booleans, null
     ensure_ascii=False)                           joined with "," and ":"
   .encode("utf-8")                                TextEncoder (UTF-8)
   hashlib.sha256                                  crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256")
   "sha256:" + hexdigest                           "sha256:" + hex
```

The test suite pins one vector; the deny-all example's hash appears on this site and in the tests, so a change to either implementation fails a build.

## 5. What the launcher adds (designed)

```
 sharness-ai launch --manifest m.json --expect-hash sha256:M -- claude …        (not built)
   1. canonicalise the manifest, hash it, refuse unless it equals M (or carries the root key's signature)
   2. for each component: useradd an ephemeral uid                                            ~49 ms, measured
   3. make a P-256 session CA; issue one certificate per role (SAN URI spiffe://<session>/<role>);
      destroy the CA key; put the CA certificate's hash in the manifest                       24 ms, measured
   4. start sharness.kms under its policy; it makes the session identity, prints k1 only; freeze it
   5. for the orchestrator: apply its Landlock domain (execute allowlist, state folder, two ports),
      drop to its uid, no_new_privs, then exec it                                             E06
   6. per command: start the other components under their policies (new namespaces ~4 ms), run, tear down
   7. at session end: thaw and kill the KMS; delete users, firewall rules, sockets
```

Steps 2, 3, 4 and 6 reuse what `run.apply` already does per process. The new pieces are the session CA (a few dozen lines with `cryptography`) and the orchestrator's domain, which is the process-tree proof of concept, E06.

Sources: the modules `cli.py`, `policy.py`, `landlock.py`, `run.py`, `hello.py` and `probe.py` on the CLI's `dev` branch, 25 Oct 2026; [Components: sharness.launcher](../../design/components/index.md#sharness-launcher); [Enforcing the process tree](../../design/process-tree/index.md).

== code/examples/index.md — Examples

# Examples

> Every runnable example, with its output as of 25 Oct 2026 in one Claude agent workspace (Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.18, Landlock ABI 7, uid 0). Nothing here is a component; each is an experiment on the [ladder](../experiments/index.md).

## Install

```
pip install git+https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI@dev     # the experiments (unreleased to PyPI)
sharness-ai --version
```

## E01: the grant

```
$ sharness-ai probe
sharness-ai probe   the grant: what a process here can do before any policy
identity    uid 0 (root) · capabilities all (CapEff 000001fffeffffff, CapBnd 000001fffeffffff) · NoNewPrivs 0 · Seccomp 0
kernel      linux 6.18.44-fc-v153 · Landlock ABI 7 · memfd_secret yes · cgroups hybrid (v1 + unified)
namespaces  cgroup, ipc, mnt, net, pid, pid_for_children, time, time_for_children, user, uts
config      CGROUP_FREEZER=y  USER_NS=y  SECCOMP=y  SECRETMEM=y  FUSE_FS=y  SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y  PKCS8_PRIVATE_KEY_PARSER=not set
tools       unshare ✔  setpriv ✔  bwrap ✗  strace ✔  iptables ✔  nft ✔  useradd ✔  fusermount3 ✗  criu ✗
egress      proxy variables set: HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, NO_PROXY, no_proxy (names only; values are never printed)
reading     this process is root with every capability and no seccomp: the grant is everything. A policy applied from here binds its children, not itself.
```

`--json` gives the same as a machine-readable object.

## E02: a policy and its hash

The deny-all example, `experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json`:

```json
{"pbp": 1, "id": "deny-all-example", "layer": "invocation",
 "notes": "E02 example: read and exec the system, write nowhere, no network. ...",
 "files": {"read": ["/usr", "/lib", "/lib64", "/bin", "/etc"], "write": [], "exec": ["/usr", "/bin"]},
 "network": "none",
 "process": {"no_new_privs": true}}
```

```
$ sharness-ai policy hash experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json
sha256:ab1d3e4e779313274f7a1d3ef3e46f6eacef038d8cfaa6198151a45cd82dcc76
$ sharness-ai policy check experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json
experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json: well-formed v0 policy, id deny-all-example: read 5 path(s), write 0, exec 2; network none; sha256:ab1d…cc76
```

Paste the same file into [the browser mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html): the hash is the same. The second example, `allow-https-example.json`, is the same policy with `"network": {"connect_tcp_ports": [443]}`.

## E03: one command under a policy

```
$ sharness-ai run --policy experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json -- /bin/sh -c 'echo "$SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_ID $SHARNESS_AI_POLICY_HASH"; touch /x; grep NoNewPrivs /proc/self/status'
deny-all-example sha256:ab1d3e4e779313274f7a1d3ef3e46f6eacef038d8cfaa6198151a45cd82dcc76
touch: cannot touch '/x': Permission denied
grep: /proc/self/status: Permission denied

$ sharness-ai run --policy experiments/policies/allow-https-example.json -- python3 -I -c "import socket; print(socket.create_connection(('1.1.1.1', 443)).getpeername())"
('1.1.1.1', 443)
$ sharness-ai run --policy experiments/policies/allow-https-example.json -- python3 -I -c "import socket; socket.create_connection(('1.1.1.1', 80))"
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied

$ sharness-ai run --policy experiments/policies/deny-all-example.json --expect-hash sha256:0000…0000 -- /bin/true
sharness-ai run: refused. The policy hashes to sha256:ab1d…cc76; the hash supplied was sha256:0000…0000. Nothing ran.
```

`/proc` is unreadable under the deny-all policy because it is not in the read list: the policy means what it says. Port 443 allowed and port 80 refused is Landlock ABI 4's TCP rule.

With caps (`"process": {"no_new_privs": true, "max_memory_mb": 64, "max_pids": 4}`), `--verbose` reports what was applied, and the fifth background process cannot be started:

```
sharness-ai run: applied {'netns': 'netns', 'landlock_abi': 7, 'paths': 7, 'missing': [], 'ports': [],
  'limits': ['cgroup1 memory.limit_in_bytes=64MiB', 'cgroup1 pids.max=4', 'RLIMIT_AS=64MiB', 'RLIMIT_NPROC=4']}
/bin/sh: 0: Cannot fork
```

## E04: the acceptance test

```
$ sharness-ai hello
sharness-ai hello   experiment E04: the memo's acceptance test, for one child process
policy      hello  sha256:ad37e58bea6f4da65656687045b33ae9977caf90feef0ff5716a44db041b35af
            read-only: /bin, /etc, /lib, /lib64, /opt, /sbin, <the workspace>, /usr, /usr/bin
            write: none · exec: system and Python · network: none · memory: 128 MiB
kernel      Landlock ABI 7 · empty network namespace: yes (uid 0)
  ✔ read       expected allowed  got allowed
  ✔ write-tmp  expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/tmp/sharness-ai-hello.tmp')
  ✔ write-cwd  expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'sharness-ai-hello.tmp')
  ✔ net        expected refused  got refused (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied)
  ✔ memory     expected refused  got refused (MemoryError)
  ✔ hash       expected refused  got refused
result      6/6 held
caveat      applied by this process to its own children: a Boundary for them, a Setting for whoever ran this, who could have skipped it. ...
```

Exit 0 when every expectation held; `--json` for the Evidence page. The hash differs per machine because the policy lists the workspace.

## sgit under a policy

sgit 0.24.0, unchanged, under a v0 policy that allows the system and the key store read-only, no writes, no network (24 Oct 2026):

```
$ sharness-ai run --policy p-sgit-ro.json -- sgit --version
sgit-ai v0.24.0
$ sharness-ai run --policy p-sgit-ro.json -- sgit pki list
No key pairs found.
```

The commands that need no key and no network run as they are: transparent mode, for those. The map of what changes for the others is on [the spectrum](../../design/spectrum/index.md#3-sgits-next-version-the-compatibility-map).

## In a Claude Code session

The skill `sharness-hello` in the CLI repository runs E01 and E04 inside a session under the design's safety rules (never touch the orchestrator, never firewall uid 0, everything as a child subtree, leave nothing behind) and reports in the site's status words. Ask the session to "run the sharness hello".

## Not examples

The mockups compute; they enforce nothing. The storyboards draw the design. Nothing on this page binds the agent that runs it: each example confines a child process of the shell it was typed into.


==============================================================================
== code/browser/index.md — Linux in the browser
==============================================================================

# Linux in the browser: how much of the harness can run in a tab?

> **Status: researched, not yet built.** Dinis Cruz's question of 25 October 2026: is there a way to run Linux in a browser and use it to verify and demonstrate this, and how much of the harness could run there? The answer, from the primary sources read that day (as of 25 Oct 2026): a real Linux kernel runs in a tab today, Landlock has no architecture dependency, and Alpine's 32-bit kernel ships with it enabled, so `sharness-ai hello` in a browser is a build, not a research problem. The rest of the harness (uids, cgroups, mutual TLS on loopback) runs in the same guest; what a browser can never show is listed at the end. This is experiment E09 on the [ladder](../experiments/index.md).

## 1. What the guest has to offer

`hello` and `run` call Landlock through syscalls 444, 445 and 446, probe `memfd_secret` as 447, and use `unshare` for the empty network namespace. So the guest needs a real Linux kernel of 6.7 or later (TCP rules, ABI 4), ideally 6.15 or later (ABI 7, the same as the measured environment), built with `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y` and `landlock` in its LSM list, user and network namespaces, cgroups, and Python 3.11 or later with `ctypes`.

Three kernel facts decide the rest, all from the kernel's own sources:

- **Landlock is architecture-independent.** `security/landlock/Kconfig` depends only on `SECURITY`; the three syscalls are in every syscall table, including the 32-bit x86 one (`444 i386 landlock_create_ruleset`). The numbers the CLI uses are the same on i386 and x86_64.
- **The ABI follows the kernel version:** 1 = 5.13, 2 = 5.19, 3 = 6.2, 4 = 6.7, 5 = 6.10, 6 = 6.12, 7 = 6.15, 8 = 7.0, 9 = 7.1 (`landlock(7)`).
- **`memfd_secret` is available on i386 in principle** (`SECRETMEM` depends on `ARCH_HAS_SET_DIRECT_MAP`, selected by x86, arm64, riscv, s390 and loongarch), with one caveat: a July 2026 kernel thread reports a crash with highmem folios on 32-bit x86, and Alpine's x86 kernel uses PAE. Not verified whether the fix is merged.

## 2. The options

| Option | Real kernel? | Arch | Kernel shipped | Landlock | seccomp, namespaces, cgroups | Python | Licence | Cost to embed on this site |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v86 + Alpine 3.23 x86** (own image) | yes | i386 only | Alpine `linux-virt` 6.18.58 | **yes**: `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y`, `landlock` first in `CONFIG_LSM`; ABI 7 expected | yes (`USER_NS`, memcg, pids, freezer) | 3.12.15 (an 8.3 MB apk) | BSD-2 (v86), distro licences | 2.4 MB runtime, no special headers, 30 to 60 MB of kernel and rootfs fetched lazily over 9p; fits GitHub Pages |
| v86 with the copy.sh Buildroot image | yes | i386 | 6.8.12 | **no** (no Landlock string in the kernel) | partly | no | BSD-2 | same; a useful negative control |
| v86 + Debian bookworm i386 | yes | i386 | 6.1.190 | ABI 2 only: no TCP rules | yes | 3.11.2 | BSD-2 | larger image |
| JSLinux (TinyEMU) x86_64 | yes | x86_64 | 6.19.3, Bellard's build | **no** (`CONFIG_SECURITY` appears off) | seccomp yes | not shown | TinyEMU MIT; the web build's terms unstated | not redistributable with confidence |
| WebVM / CheerpX 1.2.8 | **no**: syscall emulation, no kernel | 32-bit user mode | none | no | no | 3.7 (Debian buster) | engine free only for individuals and FOSS; no self-hosting | COOP/COEP headers, 600 MB streamed disk |
| container2wasm 0.8.4 (default) | yes (Bochs or TinyEMU) | x86_64, riscv64 | 6.1 | **no** (`CONFIG_SECURITY` unset in its config) | yes | any OCI image | Apache-2.0 plus LGPL Bochs | 150 to 200 MB per visitor; needs a service worker for the headers on GitHub Pages |
| container2wasm with a forked kernel ≥ 6.15 | yes | x86_64 | custom | yes (expected) | yes | any | as above | same, plus a kernel rebuild |
| qemu-wasm (QEMU 8.2) | yes | x86_64, aarch64, riscv64 | yours | depends on your kernel | yes | yours | GPL/LGPL | pthreads, SharedArrayBuffer, experimental |
| Pyodide 314 | no | Wasm | none | no | no | 3.14.2 | MPL-2.0 | one script tag; no `ctypes` syscalls at all |
| Wasmer SDK 0.19 (WASIX) | no | Wasm | none | no | no | 3.13.20 | modified MIT | COOP/COEP |
| browser_wasi_shim, jco | no | Wasm | none | capabilities instead | no | a CPython-wasi build | MIT/Apache | tiny |

The split is clean. Anything without a kernel (WebVM, Pyodide, Wasmer, WASI) cannot run Landlock, seccomp, namespaces or cgroups: there is no process in the Linux sense to confine. Anything with a kernel can, if the kernel was built with them, and of those only v86 with Alpine's kernel has Landlock on by default, runs without special response headers, and has a licence that allows self-hosting on a static site.

## 3. The recommended build: `hello` in a tab on sharness.ai

1. **Build the guest** with v86's own `tools/docker/alpine`, moving the base image from `i386/alpine:3.21.0` to `i386/alpine:3.23` (kernel 6.18.58, Landlock ABI 7, the same as the measured workspace) and adding `python3` and the `sharness_ai` package (no dependencies) to the rootfs. Keep the 9p initramfs. Snapshot the booted state with `build-state.js` so the page opens in seconds, not after a full boot.
2. **Check inside the guest:** `dmesg | grep landlock` must say "Up and running"; `sharness-ai probe` must report Landlock ABI 7, user namespaces, cgroups. Add a non-root user so the network probe exercises Landlock's TCP rule (as root, `hello` takes the network-namespace path instead).
3. **Make the network probe honest.** With no network backend in v86, a connect fails anyway. Either turn on the `fetch` or `wisp` backend and show the probe succeed without a policy and fail with `EACCES` under one, or print the errno so the refusal is attributable to Landlock. Run the same page against the copy.sh Buildroot kernel as a negative control: no Landlock, `landlock_restrict_self` returns `ENOSYS`.
4. **The page:** `libv86.mjs` and `v86.wasm` from the `v86` npm package, pinned (0.5.472 as of 25 Oct 2026, 2.4 MB, self-hosted), the BIOS files, Alpine's kernel and initramfs, the 9p filesystem index and files, and the state snapshot; an xterm.js console; `sharness-ai hello` run on the serial line at boot. Static files only; the large ones can sit on a CORS-enabled CDN, as copy.sh's do.
5. **Label the result** on Evidence as measured in "v86 0.5.472, Alpine 3.23 x86, Linux 6.18.58, browser and date", and say what it is: the same kernel code paths, on an emulated 32-bit CPU, applied by a process to its child. A Boundary for the child, a Setting for the page's guest.

A 64-bit route for later: fork container2wasm, raise its kernel to 6.15 or later with `CONFIG_SECURITY=y` and `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y`, convert `python:3.12-alpine` plus `sharness-ai`, host with a service worker for the headers. It costs 150 to 200 MB per visitor and runs slower, but it is x86_64 and keeps `memfd_secret` clear of the 32-bit caveat.

## 4. How much of the harness can run there

| Part | In the v86 guest | Honest label |
|---|---|---|
| E01 `probe`, E02 `policy hash` | yes | the same code |
| E03 `run`, E04 `hello`: Landlock files and ports, `no_new_privs`, the caps, the network namespace | yes, on the guest kernel | the same syscalls, emulated CPU |
| separate uids per component, cgroups, the freezer | yes, inside the guest | real inside the guest; says nothing about the host |
| mutual TLS over loopback between components (E05), the KMS protocol (E08), the process-tree proof of concept (E06) | yes: all of it is processes and loopback sockets | a full harness in a tab is possible |
| `memfd_secret` | kernel logic runs; the physical property it provides is meaningless against a real host | demonstrate, do not claim |
| timing figures (3.2 ms handshakes, 0.6 s `hello`) | no: single emulated core | never quote browser timings as measurements |
| real egress, hardware keys, TPM, x86_64-only behaviour, anything about the host | no | out of scope |

## 5. The WASI variant, for what it can show

Pyodide or a WASI build can show the policy pipeline without the kernel: hashing (the [mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html) does this already), validation, and a simulator of "what this policy would allow". With a WASI runtime, `files.read` maps to read-only preopened directories, `files.write` to writable ones, `network: "none"` to no sockets at all; `exec`, `no_new_privs` and scoping have no equivalent. It demonstrates deny-by-default at the host layer and the shape of the policy, with the JavaScript host as the enforcer: a Boundary for the guest, a Setting for the page. It is a different thing from the kernel demo and must be labelled as one.

## 6. Not verified

- That Alpine 3.23's i386 kernel reports ABI 7 under v86: the config says Landlock is on and 6.18 implies ABI 7, but nothing was booted for this page.
- Boot time and speed of v86 with Alpine and Python; no published figures.
- `memfd_secret` on 32-bit with PAE: the status of the July 2026 fix.
- Whether v86 needs SharedArrayBuffer: inferred from its package and build instructions, not stated by the project.
- How CheerpX answers an unknown syscall.
- The licence of the current JSLinux x86_64 web build; the JSLinux kernel inspection relies on the absence of strings in the image, not on a config file.

Sources (all read 25 Oct 2026): the kernel's [Landlock documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html), [`landlock(7)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/landlock.7.html), [`memfd_secret(2)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/memfd_secret.2.html), `security/landlock/Kconfig`, the x86 and generic syscall tables and `mm/Kconfig` in [torvalds/linux](https://github.com/torvalds/linux); [v86](https://github.com/copy/v86) (README, `docs/linux-9p-image.md`, `docs/networking.md`, `tools/docker/alpine`), the `v86` npm package 0.5.472; Alpine aports `main/linux-lts/virt.x86.config` and `main/python3/APKBUILD` for 3.21 to 3.23; Debian's 6.1.190 kernel config; [JSLinux](https://bellard.org/jslinux/) and [TinyEMU](https://bellard.org/tinyemu/); [CheerpX](https://cheerpx.io/docs/licensing) and [WebVM](https://github.com/leaningtech/webvm); [container2wasm](https://github.com/ktock/container2wasm) and its kernel configs; [qemu-wasm](https://github.com/ktock/qemu-wasm); [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/en/stable/usage/wasm-constraints.html); the [Wasmer JS SDK](https://docs.wasmer.io/sdk/wasmer-js); [browser_wasi_shim](https://github.com/bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim); [GitHub Pages limits](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits).

== code/languages/index.md — Languages
==============================================================================

# Languages

> **Status: a recommendation, as of 25 Oct 2026**, for [roadmap decision 11](../../design/roadmap/index.md#open-decisions). What each part of SHarness is written in, what it should be written in, and why. The rule behind every row: reuse what Linux and the standard library already have before writing anything, and keep each piece small enough to read in one sitting.

## What is written, and in what

| Part | Language today | Why |
|---|---|---|
| the CLI and experiments E01 to E04 | Python 3.11+, standard library only | fast to iterate; `ctypes` reaches Landlock, `unshare` and `memfd_secret` without a C extension; sgit, the first harnessed app, is Python, so the same team reads both; the design's measurements were taken in Python |
| the browser mockups | JavaScript in the page, no framework; WebCrypto for SHA-256 | the only language a browser runs; the point of the policy-hash mockup is a second implementation that must agree with the Python one |
| the storyboards | JSON data, drawn by the storyboards.sgit.ai kit (JavaScript, pinned release) | data, not code |
| this site's tools | Python standard library (generators) and Node (the gate, the kit's validator) | no build dependencies; the same pattern as the other sites in the network |

## What each component should be written in

| Component | Recommendation | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sharness.launcher` | **Python** first, a static binary later if a platform needs one | it is configuration of things the kernel already does (uids, namespaces, cgroups, certificates); the design's target is ≤ 400 lines; Python's `ssl` and the `cryptography` package make the session CA a few dozen lines | E06 onwards |
| `sharness.net`, `sharness.fs`, `sharness.llm` | **Python**, standard library plus `cryptography` where sealing is needed | each is a small server over mutual TLS with a JSON schema; Python's `ssl` module does TLS 1.3 with client certificates; the measured handshake (3.2 ms) was Python's | E05, E07 |
| `sharness.kms` | **Python v0 (E08), then Rust** | the KMS is the one place where memory hygiene decides the security: the design already notes that Python cannot guarantee erasure, that OpenSSL copies the key into its own heap, and that scrubbing `bytes` is best effort. A Rust KMS with zeroising types and `memfd_secret` through a thin syscall layer removes a class of caveats. v0 in Python first, to settle the protocol | after E08 |
| `sharness.bash` (the server) | **Python** | it is a launcher for one command at a time: cgroup, namespaces, uid, Landlock, exec, filter | E06 |
| `sharness-bash-client` | **a small static binary: Rust or Go** | the design requires it: the orchestrator's execute allowlist must not include an interpreter, and a static binary needs none. Rust for size and no runtime; Go if the team prefers it | E06 |
| the seccomp filters | **data** (a syscall list per component in the policy), compiled to BPF by a few lines of Python; libseccomp if available, raw BPF through `ctypes` if not | the filter is part of the policy and hashed with it | the next rows of [Containment](../../design/containment/index.md) |
| the policy language | **JSON** (canonical, hashed); YAML only for reading on the site | two implementations already agree on the bytes; a policy language is explicitly not wanted ([Components](../../design/components/index.md#as-little-code-as-possible)) | now |
| the Messages API front of `sharness.llm` | Python, then whatever the platform wants when it runs the component as a service | the API is HTTP and JSON; nothing language-specific | E07 |
| the browser experiments (a Linux kernel in a tab) | JavaScript and WebAssembly around an existing emulator; the kernel and rootfs built with the normal Linux toolchain | a page on this is being researched | planned |

## Two rules that follow

1. **Python until a caveat says otherwise.** Every component starts in Python because the experiments do and because the design's own figures were measured there. A component moves to Rust only for a stated reason (memory hygiene in the KMS; a static binary for the bash client), recorded on the roadmap.
2. **No runtime dependencies in the CLI** beyond `cryptography` for the components that seal and sign. The experiments stay standard-library only so a Claude session can install and run them anywhere Python is.

## What this does not decide

Whether the platform-provided versions of the components (topology E) share any code with these; the design says only that the protocol is the same. And nothing here is a commitment of sgit's maintainers about sgit's own language, which is Python today.

Sources: [Components: as little code as possible](../../design/components/index.md#as-little-code-as-possible); [Keys §7, memory hygiene](../../design/keys/index.md#7-where-the-private-key-lives-and-for-how-long); [Enforcing the process tree §2](../../design/process-tree/index.md#2-design) (the client as a static binary); the CLI's `CLAUDE.md`.

== evidence/index.md — Evidence

# Evidence

> **Every figure on this page was observed as of 24 Oct 2026, in one Claude agent workspace (claude.ai, cloud session).** One environment, one day. Re-run the probes before relying on them elsewhere: other platforms, and later versions of this one, may differ.

Three labels are used across the site, and this page is where they are earned:

| Label | Means |
|---|---|
| **measured** | probed or timed in the environment below, with the method stated |
| **designed / proposed** | a description of how SHarness would work; nothing is built |
| **not yet measured** | named in the design, not tested: seccomp filters, read-only bind mounts, every side door on [Enforcing the process tree](../design/process-tree/index.md), and AWS KMS compatibility |

## 1. The environment

| Fact | Observed |
|---|---|
| Isolation | Firecracker microVM; PID 1 is `/process_api --firecracker-init …` (not systemd) |
| OS / kernel | Ubuntu 24.04.5, Linux 6.18.44, x86_64 |
| Agent's identity | **uid 0 (root)**, full capability set (`CapEff 000001fffeffffff`) |
| Hardening present | no seccomp, `NoNewPrivs 0`, no Yama (`/proc/sys/kernel/yama` absent) |
| Core dumps | `ulimit -c 0`; `core_pattern = core` |
| Python / crypto | Python 3.13.17; `cryptography` 50.0.1 |
| sgit | `pip install sgit-ai` → **0.24.0** (the version the origin article analysed, at commit `182cfc1`) |
| Hardware keys | no `/dev/tpm*` |
| Egress | every outbound HTTPS goes through a platform proxy at `127.0.0.1:43305`; `send.sgraph.ai`, `pki.sgit.ai`, `cli.sgit.ai` reachable (HTTP 200) |
| Scratch space | the agent's scratchpad is root-only (other uids get `EACCES`) |
| Process lifetime | per the platform: a process detached with `nohup`/`&` is stopped within minutes of the agent's reply; a tool-managed background process can run up to 2 h. **Not measured** |
| Firewall tools | `iptables`, `nft` present; OUTPUT policy ACCEPT, empty |
| cgroups | v1: blkio, cpu, cpuacct, cpuset, devices, freezer, memory, pids, systemd, unified |
| FUSE | `/dev/fuse` (root-only), `fusermount3` present |

### Kernel configuration (`/proc/config.gz`)

| Option | Value | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK` | y (ABI 7) | file and TCP port sandboxing |
| `CONFIG_SECCOMP` | y | syscall allowlists |
| `CONFIG_SECRETMEM` | y | `memfd_secret` |
| `CONFIG_CGROUP_FREEZER` | y | freeze the KMS between calls |
| `CONFIG_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` | y | CRIU possible (binary not installed) |
| `CONFIG_FUSE_FS` | y | `sharness.fs` as a mount |
| `CONFIG_ASYMMETRIC_KEY_TYPE` | y | kernel asymmetric keys … |
| `CONFIG_PKCS8_PRIVATE_KEY_PARSER` | **not set** | … but no private keys, so kernel-held decryption is unavailable |
| `CONFIG_TRUSTED_KEYS` | not set | (needs a TPM anyway) |
| `CONFIG_ENCRYPTED_KEYS` | y | symmetric blobs only |

## 2. sgit 0.24.0, checked

| Claim (from the origin article) | Result | Method |
|---|---|---|
| `pki keygen` makes RSA-OAEP 4096 + ECDSA P-256, `sha256:` + 16 hex | ✔ | ran it with a throwaway HOME |
| private keys encrypted with PBKDF2 at **2,048** iterations | ✔ `INTEGER :0800` on both `private_key.pem` and `signing_private.pem` | `openssl asn1parse` |
| `Secrets__Store` uses a fixed salt | ✔ `salt = f'{SECRETS_SALT_PREFIX}:master'` | source |
| `BestAvailableEncryption` used for keys | ✔ `crypto/PKI__Crypto.py:37` | source |
| the vault key is read in many places | 65 references in 23 files for `_read_vault_key\|load_vault_key\|vault_key_path` (broad grep including imports; the article counts 27 read sites in 17 files) | grep |
| key file modes | `public_key.pem` 0644; private PEMs 0600 | `ls -l` |

## 3. Memory

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)`, then root reads `/proc/<pid>/mem` | **secret found**: root's `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` overrides |
| `mlock` / `mlockall` | succeed |
| `memfd_secret` (syscall 447) | available |
| root reads a `memfd_secret` page through `/proc/<pid>/mem` | **`EIO`** |
| RSA-4096 OAEP open → copy into a secret page → **no** scrub; root sweeps all readable mappings | one copy found in the anonymous heap |
| the same, **with** scrubbing the returned `bytes` | **no copy found** |
| RSA-4096 OAEP open time | 3.2–3.6 ms |
| kernel keyring `add_key` (process keyring) | works |
| user keyring entry persists across separate agent tool calls | ✔ |
| key in uid `sgit-dec`'s user keyring, searched by uid `sgit-run` | `ENOKEY` |
| that key in root's `/proc/keys` | not listed |
| `add_key("asymmetric", <PKCS#8 RSA-4096 DER>)` | **`EBADMSG`** (parser not built) |
| cgroup freezer: freeze / thaw a process (average of 20) | **0.28 ms / 0.13 ms**; frozen state `D` |

## 4. Process isolation

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| create system users (`useradd -r -M -s nologin`) | ✔ |
| `setpriv --reuid --regid --clear-groups --no-new-privs --inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all` | CapEff 0, CapBnd 0, NoNewPrivs 1 |
| another uid reads a root file | denied |
| `unshare --net`, then connect out | `ENETUNREACH` (101) |
| `unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc` | ✔ |
| Landlock ABI | 7 |
| `RLIMIT_NPROC=0`, then `fork` | `EAGAIN` (blocked) |
| Landlock fs (read-only `/usr /etc /lib /lib64 /proc`): read `/etc/hostname` | allowed |
| Landlock fs: read a file elsewhere | `EACCES` |
| Landlock fs: write `/tmp/x` | `EACCES` |
| Landlock net (connect only to 43305): proxy port | allowed |
| Landlock net: `127.0.0.1:22`, `1.1.1.1:443` | `EACCES` |
| `iptables -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner <user> -j REJECT` | accepted |
| `SO_PEERCRED` on a Unix socket | returns pid, uid, gid |
| abstract-namespace Unix socket | ✔ |
| ephemeral user + firewall rule + locked launch + teardown (average of 10) | **49 ms** |
| new net + pid + mount namespaces (average of 10) | **3.7 ms** |
| seccomp filter | available, **not tested** |

## 5. Footprint

`strace -f` (file, network, process, ipc), successful opens only.

| Command | Paths opened | Folders | Distinct syscalls | execve | socket / connect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `python3 -I -c print(1)` | 39 | 21 | 31 | 1 | 0 |
| `sgit --version` | 1,104 | 212 | 38 | 1 | 0 |
| `sgit pki list` | 1,109 | 215 | 39 | 1 | 0 |
| `import sgit_ai.cli.CLI__Main` | 529 modules, 146 ms | | | | |
| bare `python3 -I -c pass` start | 15 ms | | | | |

## 6. Transport

Python `ssl`, TLS 1.3, P-256; the server is a thread in the benchmark process.

| | Connect + handshake | 600 B round trip | Bulk (64 MiB echo) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TCP plain | 0.10 ms | 15 µs | ~300 MB/s |
| TCP mutual TLS | **3.2 ms** | 67 µs | ~320 MB/s |
| Unix plain | 0.09 ms | 56 µs | ~320 MB/s |
| Unix mutual TLS | 3.4 ms | 74 µs | ~420 MB/s |
| pipe to a separate process | — | 34 µs | — |
| TCP mutual TLS **without** server `TCP_NODELAY` | 46 ms | | |

Session CA + four role certificates (P-256, 2 h validity): **24 ms**.

Edge enforcement with roles in `subjectAltName` URIs, policy `fs←{cli}, net←{cli}, kms←{net}` (the probe named the app role `cli`, as sgit's CLI):

```
cli → fs   OK        fs  → kms  DENY
cli → net  OK        cli → kms  DENY
net → kms  OK        fs  → net  DENY
```

Figures are from the final of three runs. Across runs, round trips and bulk varied by up to ~25% (TCP mutual TLS bulk: 250, 275, 318 MB/s; Unix mutual TLS bulk: 349, 378, 418 MB/s); handshake times were stable. Microsecond figures are noisy because the server thread shares Python's interpreter lock with the client: treat them as upper bounds.

## 7. The agent loop in this environment (read-only observation)

Observed as of 24 Oct 2026; may differ elsewhere. Method: `ps --forest`, `/proc/net/tcp` mapped to socket inodes, environment variable **names** only, `findmnt`. TLS traffic was not inspected, no credentials or session identifiers were captured, and no configuration was changed.

| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| PID 1 | `/process_api --firecracker-init … --block-local-connections` |
| PID 89 | `environment-manager task-run --stdin …`, root; its own HTTPS connections to the model API address |
| PID 96 | `/opt/claude-code/bin/claude`, Claude Code **2.1.42**, root; ~18 established HTTPS connections to the model API address; listens on a local port |
| the agent's Bash | direct child of PID 96 |
| other processes | `sbx-telemetry-collector` (own uid), `rclone-filestore multimount` |
| model endpoint | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com`; `/etc/hosts` pins it; it is in `no_proxy`, so model calls bypass the egress proxy |
| credentials | carried in `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`; value **deliberately not read** |
| harness flags (names / booleans only) | `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1`, `CCR_AGENT_PROXY_ENABLED=1`, `CCR_UPSTREAM_PROXY_ENABLED=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_RESOLVES_HOSTS=true` |
| `/opt/claude-code` | read-only mount |
| `/root/.claude/settings.json` | writable by root; no managed settings under `/etc/claude-code/` |
| `/etc/hosts` | writable by root; its mtime changed mid-session |
| kernel cmdline | `nomodule` |

## 8. Left in the environment

The probes left users `sgit-dec` and `sgit-run`, a folder of probe scripts (`/opt/sgit-probe/`) and a user-keyring entry `sgit:persist-probe` (root). All died with the VM.

## 9. The first experiments, run by the CLI

Run on 24 October 2026 in a second Claude Code cloud session (as of 24 Oct 2026). The commands are experiments E01 to E04 in the CLI repository, [experiments/README.md](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md); the map is [Mockups and experiments](../code/experiments/index.md). Method: `sharness-ai probe` for the environment (read-only; it prints the names of proxy variables, never values), `sharness-ai hello --json` for the result; each probe is `python3 -I -c …` run as a child under the policy by `sharness-ai run`.

| Fact | Observed (E01, probe) |
|---|---|
| Environment | Ubuntu 24.04.5, Linux 6.18.44, Python 3.13.17; uid 0, every capability, `NoNewPrivs 0`, `Seccomp 0` |
| Kernel | Landlock ABI 7; `memfd_secret` available; cgroups v1 with a unified mount; `CONFIG_PKCS8_PRIVATE_KEY_PARSER` not set |
| Tools | `unshare`, `setpriv`, `strace`, `iptables`, `nft`, `useradd` present; `bwrap`, `fusermount3`, `criu` absent |
| Egress | `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` set (names only); the proxy port differed from the one seen in §7 |
| Harness | Claude Code **2.1.310** (§7 observed 2.1.42 on the same day in another session): versions move between sessions |

| Probe (E04, `hello`) | Policy says | Result |
|---|---|---|
| list `/usr` | allowed | allowed |
| create `/tmp/sharness-ai-hello.tmp` | refused | `EACCES` (Landlock) |
| create a file in the workspace | refused | `EACCES` (Landlock) |
| TCP connect to `1.1.1.1:443` | refused | `EACCES` (Landlock port rule; an empty network namespace was also applied) |
| run with a wrong `--expect-hash` | refused, nothing runs | exit 125, nothing ran |

Policy hash `sha256:ad37e58bea6f4da65656687045b33ae9977caf90feef0ff5716a44db041b35af` (the `hello` policy generated for that interpreter; the paths include the workspace, so the hash differs per machine). 5 of 5 held; the whole run took 0.6 s. Under E03 with the `allow-https-example` policy, a connect to `1.1.1.1:443` succeeded and one to port 80 was refused.

**Caps, measured 25 Oct 2026** (as of 25 Oct 2026, the same kind of session; cgroups v1 with a unified mount). `process.max_memory_mb` and `process.max_pids` in a v0 policy are applied by `sharness-ai run` as `RLIMIT_AS` and `RLIMIT_NPROC` on the child plus a memory and a pids cgroup under `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/sharness-ai/<pid>` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/pids/sharness-ai/<pid>`, removed by the parent afterwards:

| Probe | Policy says | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bytearray(400 << 20)` under `max_memory_mb: 128` (E04, `hello`, now 6 probes) | refused | `MemoryError` (the rlimit fires first; the cgroup would OOM-kill) |
| `bytearray(8 << 20)` under the same cap | allowed | allowed |
| the fifth background process under `max_pids: 4` | refused | `Cannot fork` from the shell |
| cgroup left behind after the run | none | none (the per-pid directories and the empty parent are removed) |

`hello` with the memory probe: 6 of 6 held. Not yet: the `cpu` cgroup, `max_runtime_s`, seccomp.

**What this does not show.** The policy was applied by the session to its own children. It is a Boundary for them and a Setting for the session (the same root process that could have skipped it). It says nothing about seccomp, uids, cgroups, mutual TLS or the process tree, none of which the experiments touch yet.

## Documented, not yet exercised

- A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook can replace a tool's input before it runs (`updatedInput`, documented 24 Oct 2026), which answers [Agents §2](../design/agents/index.md#2-where-sharness-plugs-in) row 3. Not yet exercised on a pinned version.

## Not yet measured

- seccomp filters (available in the kernel; no filter tested)
- read-only bind mounts (namespaces tested; read-only binds not separately)
- every side door on [Enforcing the process tree](../design/process-tree/index.md): the proof of concept has not been run
- AWS KMS asymmetric RSA-4096 with OAEP-SHA-256 matching sgit's envelope
- the experiments E01 to E04 on a laptop (no root; on Ubuntu 24.04 an unprivileged user namespace may be refused, so `network: "none"` falls back to Landlock's TCP rules, which do not cover UDP)

Source: [04-environment-evidence](../project/sources/sharness-brief-pack/docs/04-environment-evidence.md); §9 from the CLI's experiments, run 24 Oct 2026.

# What exists today, and what does not

> **The honest column, as of 25 Oct 2026.** SHarness is at the design stage with the first experiments runnable. What exists as running code is listed here and kept apart from the design, so a reader, human or agent, can tell what they can rely on.

## Exists, and can be checked

| Thing | Where to check it |
|---|---|
| **The `sharness-ai` package on PyPI**, v0.1.0: reports its version and prints its help | [pypi.org/project/sharness-ai](https://pypi.org/project/sharness-ai/) |
| **Experiments E01 to E04 and E10** (`probe`, `policy hash`, `run`, `hello`, `policy translate`), with 40 tests, on the CLI's `dev` branch; unreleased to PyPI | [the code](../../code/index.md) · [experiments/README.md](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md) · E04 measured on [Evidence §9](../index.md#9-the-first-experiments-run-by-the-cli) |
| **Two example policies and a skill** for Claude Code sessions | [Examples](../../code/examples/index.md) |
| **Two browser mockups** that compute and enforce nothing | [the policy hash](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html) (the same hash as the CLI) · [the edge matrix](../../explain/mockups/edges.html) |
| **Three storyboards**, data drawn by the storyboards.sgit.ai kit | [Storyboards](../../explain/storyboards/index.md); what they show is the design, not something built |
| **The design, published for review**, with the brief and four drawn diagrams | [The brief](../../design/index.md) · [the source documents, verbatim](../../project/sources/index.md) |
| **Measurements behind the design** | [Evidence](../index.md): one Claude agent workspace, with method and date |
| **This site, its gate and its deploy pipeline** | [SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__Website](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__Website) · [how it is built](../../project/engineering.html) |

## Not here yet

| Missing | Status |
|---|---|
| **Any SHarness component** (launcher, kms, net, fs, bash, llm) | Not built. Designed on [Components](../../design/components/index.md). |
| **A CLI release beyond `--version`** | v0.1.0 on PyPI is the skeleton and the pipeline; the experiments are on `dev`, unreleased ([R7](../../project/comms.html#r7)). |
| **The launcher above the agent** | Not built. Every experiment applies a policy to a child process; nothing yet binds the agent itself. |
| **The process-tree proof of concept** (E06) | Started, not completed, not run. See [Enforcing the process tree](../../design/process-tree/index.md). |
| **seccomp, the `cpu` cgroup, read-only binds** | Available in the measured kernel; not yet applied by the CLI or measured (memory and pids caps are, since 25 Oct 2026). See [Containment](../../design/containment/index.md). |
| **The newsroom's agents' policies** | The second user in the memo; their file and network behaviour policies are not written. |
| **Markdown twins for the hand-written pages** | Every page has a twin except the front page's sections, the mockups and the three project pages (engineering, comms, releases). |

# Research note: the published design, read in full

> **Status: a review, as of 24 Oct 2026.** Everything published about SHarness was read end to end by a second agent session on 24 October 2026: the eleven design pages, the two articles, the memo, the eight documents of the design pack, the CLI repository, and the sites and documentation the design points at. This page says what holds up, what to improve, what was improved in this release, and what is still open. Written by sharness.build; the editorial responsibility is Dinis Cruz's.

## 1. What was read

| Source | What | Read |
|---|---|---|
| sharness.ai v0.3.1 | the front page, eleven design pages with their markdown twins, `llms.txt`, the honest column, the CLI page, comms and release history | all of it |
| the two articles | *A secure harness for agents* (from voice memo 01) and *What shipped on day one* | both, and the memo transcript |
| the design pack | the brief for the site and documents 00 to 07, verbatim under `briefs/` | all eight, against the pages ported from them |
| SHarness-AI__CLI | `dev` at commit `0a53a7c`: the package skeleton, the pipeline, the README | all of it |
| storyboards.sgit.ai and api.storyboards.sgit.ai | the format, the quick start, the render guide, the catalogue, the pki series' storyboards and cast, the site repository's README | the parts needed to author storyboards for this site |
| Claude Code documentation | hooks (`PreToolUse`, `updatedInput`), permissions (deny rules, `Bash` as a bare deny), sandboxing | the pages, 24 Oct 2026 |
| this session's own environment | the grant, with the probe (E01): uid 0, all capabilities, Landlock ABI 7, `memfd_secret`, Claude Code 2.1.310 | read-only, names of variables only |

## 2. What holds up

- **The claim labels.** *Measured*, *designed*, *not yet measured*, each with a date and a method, on every page. Nothing read on the site claims to be built. This is rarer than it should be and is the site's main asset; everything in this release keeps it.
- **The threat model is stated and kept to.** Kernel trusted, root out of scope, said on every page where it matters, and the one row of the prompt-injection walkthrough that is *not stopped locally* is printed in the same table as the rows that are.
- **The architecture is one idea applied consistently.** One role, one uid, one policy, one certificate; the edge matrix; the KMS that never returns a clear key; the hash from outside the agent. The pages agree with each other and with the pack.
- **Markdown twins and `llms.txt`.** An agent reads the same text as a person, and the gate fails the release if they drift. The storyboards in this release follow the same rule.
- **The evidence is reproducible in shape.** Each figure has a method; the probes' leftovers are listed; the variance between runs is given.

## 3. What to improve, and what this release did about it

| # | Finding | Done in v0.4.0 | Still open |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Nothing was runnable.** The design asked for *very simple examples first* and the package did nothing. | E01 to E04 in the CLI (`probe`, `policy hash`, `run`, `hello`), with tests; E04 measured; the ladder on [Mockups and experiments](../../code/experiments/index.md) | E05 to E08; the launcher |
| 2 | **Claude Code's own sandbox was missing from the design** as prior art and as a plug-in point. It does, for Bash, much of what `sharness.bash` would do, and its documented limits (hooks, MCP servers and excluded commands run unsandboxed; hostname-only filtering; an unsandboxed retry) are exactly the side doors the design lists. | the comparison on [Mockups and experiments](../../code/experiments/index.md#what-claude-codes-own-sandbox-already-gives-and-what-sharness-adds); rows on [Agents and LLMs §2](../../design/agents/index.md#2-where-sharness-plugs-in) and [Policies §9](../../design/policies/index.md#9-prior-art-reuse-dont-rebuild) | generating the sandbox's settings from a policy, as one enforcement layer |
| 3 | **An open question had been answered by the documentation.** Agents §2 said a `PreToolUse` hook rewriting a Bash call was *believed yes: verify*. The hooks documentation (read 24 Oct 2026) states `updatedInput` replaces the whole tool input before it runs, and permission rules are evaluated against the rewritten input. | Agents §2 updated; the item moved off Evidence's not-yet-measured list as *documented, not yet exercised* | exercising it on a pinned version |
| 4 | **The policy schema had no version two implementations could hash.** The full schema on Policies §4 is right as a target and too large to start with. | a v0 shape (six keys, integers only) hashed identically by the CLI and by the [browser mockup](../../explain/mockups/policy-hash.html); on [The CLI](../../code/cli/index.md#the-v0-policy) | layers by intersection; signing by the root key |
| 5 | **The design had no short form.** Eleven pages, no way in for someone with ten minutes. | three [storyboards](../../explain/storyboards/index.md) in the storyboards.sgit.ai kit: the last metre, its one job, hello world inside; each with a markdown script | a fourth on the KMS protocol; the series listed on storyboards.sgit.ai |
| 6 | **The site repository's README called the command `sharness`.** The site and the roadmap say `sharness-ai`. | fixed | |
| 7 | **The CLI page was hand-written HTML with no markdown twin**, listed as missing on the honest column. | the page is now markdown, generated like the design pages | the status and admin pages still have no twin |
| 8 | **The memo's *maybe a skill* had no concrete answer.** | the `sharness-hello` skill in the CLI repository runs E01 and E04 inside a session under the safety rules, and says every time what it does not bind | a skill that installs a launcher above the session: not possible from inside it |
| 9 | **The observed environment moves.** Evidence §7 observed Claude Code 2.1.42; this session ran 2.1.310, with the egress proxy on a different port. Figures tied to a version need the version beside them. | noted on Evidence §9 | re-run the §7 observation when the design is next revised |
| 10 | **Two small things in the published pack** (a broken link, `harness.<role>` in one diagram) are known and listed. | unchanged, by the rule that the pack is verbatim | fix in the pack's next revision (T2) |

## 4. What is still open, in the order to take it

1. **E06, the process-tree proof of concept.** It is the one experiment the design marks *not yet run*, and it decides whether `sharness.bash` can be made impossible to skip. Run it under the safety rules, in a child subtree, and publish every side door's result on Evidence.
2. **E05, the edges as a script.** The mutual TLS measurements exist; making them a command makes them repeatable on a laptop and in Docker.
3. **E08 before E07.** `sharness.llm` needs the real API key from somewhere; a local `sharness.kms` v0 that opens a sealed `m1` and re-seals derived keys is the smaller piece and unblocks the other.
4. **The launcher, as a script above the agent, on a laptop.** The first place the caveat printed by `hello` stops applying: a script starts Claude Code under a policy it cannot widen. Disposable users per session, measured at about 49 ms each in the cloud workspace, belong here.
5. **Policies for the newsroom's agents.** The memo's second user. Their file and network behaviour policies written down are the first real test of the schema.
6. **seccomp, read-only bind mounts, AWS KMS compatibility**: still on the not-yet-measured list.

## 5. What this note does not claim

- The review is one agent's reading on one day. R3 on the [comms board](../../project/comms.html), a review of the design pages by a person, is still open.
- Nothing measured here changes the design's figures; it adds one experiment's result in one environment.
- The comparison with Claude Code's sandbox is against its documentation on 24 Oct 2026, not against its code, and says nothing about any platform's plans.

Sources: every page of this site at v0.3.1; the design pack under [the source documents](../../project/sources/index.md); [experiments/README.md](https://github.com/SHarness-AI/SHarness-AI__CLI/blob/dev/experiments/README.md); the Claude Code documentation on [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) and [sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing); [api.storyboards.sgit.ai/docs](https://api.storyboards.sgit.ai/docs/index.html).
